newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Analysis of key elements in Wednesday's European Champions' League matches:
Group A
Ajax Amsterdam (Netherlands) v Auxerre (France)

Ajax are still crippled by injuries but need just a point to clinch a place in the quarter-finals. Jari Litmanen, scorer of the winning goal in the match in Auxerre, is still out, as are skipper Danny Blind, Winston Bogarde, Peter Hoekstra and Richard Witschge. Kiki Musampa and Arnold Scholten, who scored his first European Cup goal in the 1-0 win against Glasgow Rangers, are also doubtful starters. Brazilian defender Santos is suspended after picking up two yellow cards.

Auxerre, who must win to have any realistic chance of a quarter-final place, will be without international midfielder Sabri Lamouchi, young striker Thomas Deniaud, Australian defender Ned Zelic and strikers Antoine Sibierski and Lilian Laslandes. France international Alain Goma is suspended. The French champions have taken only one point from their last three league games. Defeat on Wednesday would end their season in Europe.
Glasgow Rangers (Scotland) v Grasshopper Zurich (Switzerland)

England midfielder Paul Gascoigne is serving the second match of a four-match ban for kicking Ajax's Winston Bogarde in a match last month. Rangers are the only side in the competition without a point and have already been eliminated. Their main aim on Wednesday will be to avenge their 3-0 defeat in Switzerland two months ago.

Grasshoppers are without defender Harald Gamperle for the rest of the season after he underwent surgery this week. Forward Viorel Moldovan and midfielder Murat Yakin are both suspended after picking up second yellow cards in their last game against Auxerre. Yakin scored the only goal in Grasshopper's 1-0 win over Ajax while Moldovan tops the Swiss scoring table with 17 goals. The Swiss champions will rely more than ever on Nestor Subiat and Kubilay Turkyilmaz.
Group B
Steaua Bucharest (Romania) v Atletico Madrid (Spain)

Defenders Tudorel Zamfirescu and Tiberiu Csik are suspended with two yellow cards each and a demoralised Steaua have long since lost any hope of qualification for the last eight. They prop up Group B and financial difficulties have recently forced them to sell two of their best players -- Adrian Ilie and Iulien Filipescu -- to Galatasaray.

Atletico have hit form, following their epic 3-3 draw with Barcelona nine days ago with a 2-1 defeat of Espanyol. Influential defender Santi Denia, who scored his first-ever goal for the club on Saturday, is out injured -- Juan Lopez is expected to fill the gap -- and set-piece specialist Milinko Pantic faces a late fitness test (twisted ankle). The Spaniards won the first clash against Steaua in Madrid 4-0.
Widzew Lodz (Poland) v Borussia Dortmund (Germany)

Widzew Lodz went top of the Polish league at the weekend by beating previous leaders Legia Warsaw 1-0 and are playing with more fluency than last time they met the Germans, when they lost 2-1. But they have virtually no chance of qualifying despite beating Steaua Bucharest in their last European match.

Dortmund hope to have Matthias Sammer back in the starting line-up after an eight-week layoff (leg muscle tear). The libero made his comeback as a second half substitute in Saturday's 1-1 draw with Karlsruhe. Defender Martin Kree is also due back from injury. Striker Heiko Herrlich is doubtful (ligament damage) but coach Ottmar Hitzfeld has vowed to seek an away win to secure first place in the group.
Group C
Fenerbahce (Turkey) v Rapid Vienna (Austria)

Fenerbahce look to repeat their historic victory over Manchester United at Old Trafford in their last match. Bulgarian striker Emil Kostadinov and exciting Nigerian forward Jay Jay Okocha were among eight players slightly injured in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Istanbulspor but both are expected to play. Bosnian Elvir Bolic, the Turks' hero at Old Trafford, scored Fenerbahce's equaliser at the weekend and will again be key.

Rapid, mauled 5-0 by Juventus on their last European outing, warmed up for Wednesday's clash by beating first division rivals Ried 6-0. Polish defender Andrzej Lesiak returns to the squad after missing the match in Turin (knee injury). He scored the equaliser against Juve in their clash in Austria in October to give Rapid one of only two Champions' League points to date.
Manchester United (England) v Juventus (Italy)

Welsh winger Ryan Giggs is back after lengthy injury, as is Irishman Roy Keane. United are expected to recall defender Denis Irwin, who missed the 1-0 league defeat of Arsenal on Saturday. One of the two Neville brothers looks sure to be dropped instead. Czech international Karel Poborsky may also miss out now Giggs is back. United need at least a point to keep their quarter-final bid on course.

Juve defenders Paolo Montero of Uruguay and Ciro Ferrara, both suspended for their side's 0-0 draw with Milan at the weekend, are expected to return, probably in place of Mark Juliano and Alessio Tacchinardi. Gifted playmaker Alessandro Del Piero, who came on as an 85th minute substitute against Milan, may again be sacrificed for a 4-4-2 Juventus line-up in which Croat Alen Boksic will be partnered by either Michele Padovano or Christian Vieri.
Group D
Rosenborg Trondheim (Norway) v IFK Gothenburg (Sweden)

The two Scandinavian sides are level on three points each and both need a win to keep alive their hopes of advancing to the next round. Rosenborg had to travel to Denmark to train because of snow and freezing temperatures at home, but the weather has since improved. Veteran defender Karl Petter Loeken may be sidelined (shoulder injury). Forward Jan-Ivar "Mini" Jakobsen was sent off in Rosenborg's last match and is suspended.

Gothenburg, who lost the first clash between the two sides 3-2, are at full strength and can name top player Jesper Blomqvist who signed for Group D rivals AC Milan last week. Under his contract Blomqvist can play against the Norwegians, and against group leaders Porto on December 4, before joining the Italian champions.
Porto (Portugal) v AC Milan (Italy)

Porto, who beat Milan 3-2 in the sides' first clash in Italy, are looking for a fifth straight Champions' League win to clinch first spot in group D, from which they have already qualified. The club has been caught up in allegations of attempted match-fixing and bribery 12 years ago but beat Rio Ave 1-0 away at the weekend to stay top of the league. Defender Paulo Santos is suspended with two yellow cards, otherwise Porto are at full strength.

Second-placed Milan are still not guaranteed a quarter-final place and sorely need a result in Portugal. Frenchman Marcel Desailly and Christian Panucci, who both missed their side's 0-0 draw against Juventus on Sunday, may return in place of Dutchman Michael Reiziger and Stefano Eranio respectively.
